## Part A — Creating Vectors and List

Question 1

Create a vector for the worker’s age.
(age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)
)

How many data points?
([1] 50)

c: Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker’s age.
([1] 17
[1] 61)

Access the 13rd to 18th elements and 33th to 35th elements of worker’s Age.
([1] 27 22 37 34 19 20 33 41 53)

Access all but the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements are not included.
( [1] 34 28 22  0 27 18 52 39 42 29 35 31 27  0 37 34 19 20 57 49 50 37 46  0 17 37 43 53 41
[30] 51 35 24 33 41 53 40 18 44 38 41 48 27 39  0 30 61 54 58 26 18)

f: Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0.
([1] 34 28 22  0 27 18 52 39 42 29 35 31 27  0 37 34 19 20 57 49 50 37 46  0 17 37 43 53 41
[30] 51 35 24 33 41 53 40 18 44 38 41 48 27 39  0 30 61 54 58 26 18)

```{r}
age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

length(age)

min(age)
max(age)

age[c(13:18, 33:35)]

age[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]

age[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0
age
```

Question 3

-Create vectors according to the above table.

```{r}
power_ranking <- 1:25

celebrity_name <- c("Tom Cruise", "Rolling Stones", "Oprah Winfrey", "U2", "Tiger Woods", "Steven Spielberg", "Howard Stern", "50 Cent", "Cast of the Sopranos", "Dan Brown", "Bruce Springsteen", "Donald Trump", "Muhammad Ali", "Paul McCartney", "George Lucas", "Elton John", "David Letterman", "Phil Mickelson", "J.K Rowling", "Bradd Pitt", "Peter Jackson", "Dr. Phil McGraw", "Jay Leno", "Celine Dion", "Kobe Bryant")

pay <- c(67, 90, 225, 110, 90, 332, 302, 41, 52, 88, 55, 44, 55, 40, 233, 34, 40, 47, 75, 25, 39, 45, 32, 40, 31)
```

b. Modify the power ranking and pay of J.K. Rowling. Change power ranking to 15 and pay to 90.

```{r}
index <- which(celebrity_name == "J.K Rowling")

power_ranking[index] <- 15
pay[index] <- 90

power_ranking
pay
```

Question 4

- Create a list of ten (10) vegetables you ate during your lifetime. If none, just list down the vegetables in your mind.

```{r}
vegetables <- list("Cabbage", "Squash", "Spinach", "Carrot", "Eggplant", "Bittergourd", "Moringa", "Potato", "Cucumber", "Beans")
vegetables

vegetables <- append(vegetables, list("Bamboo Shoots", "Bell Pepper"))
vegetables

length(vegetables)

vegetables <- append(vegetables, c("Corn", "Papaya", "Asparagus", "Pumpkin"), after = 5)
vegetables
```

a. Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetables in the list. What is the result
b. How many datapoints do you have?
c. Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5. What is the result?
d. How many datapoints does your vegetable list have?
